author: agent-3
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO. No second-party review. See threat-model.v1.json#reviewStatus.
purpose: Close the two remaining runtime-behaviour domains: observability (what the system says about itself) and validation gates (what must be true before a release ships).

decisionDependencies.claim: telemetry is never evidence and never enters the digest
diagnostics are an exfiltration channel and must be budgeted
every exportable artifact carries a privacy class
release gates include a no-flake policy

planes.content: The sealed Run: findings, Coverage, verdict, provenance, digest
planes.rule: The only plane whose content is authoritative. Nothing else may influence a verdict.

planes.content: Structured stage/unit events for live rendering
planes.rule: Producers emit structured events, never free-form output. A no-op sink must be valid and must not change results.

planes.content: Bounded, typed explanations attached to or referenced by a Run
planes.durability: referenced by the Run, subject to retention
planes.rule: Bounded by budget and privacy class. This is the plane TM.F3 attacks, so bandwidth is a resource, not a courtesy.
Off by default. No phone-home. Local profiling must work with no exporter configured — observing your own tool must not require a network.

correlation.key: ExecutionId on every event in every plane, plus parent Run identity for multi-stage work
correlation.rule: An event that cannot be correlated to an execution is a defect, not a log line.
correlation.why: Under agent-loop concurrency, several executions interleave in one terminal and one ledger. Uncorrelated output is unreadable and unattributable.

volumeBudgets.rule: Every plane except evidence carries a per-Run budget on count and total size.
volumeBudgets.onExhaustion: Truncate with a visible, typed marker stating what was dropped and why. Silent truncation is the failure this whole architecture is built against.
volumeBudgets.why: Two independent reasons: an agent loop or CI log drowned in per-fact output is unusable, and TM.F3 makes diagnostics bandwidth an exfiltration channel.

producerOutput.rule: Producer stderr is captured, bounded, and attributed. It is NEVER a public contract.
producerOutput.why: A contribution that discovers its stderr is parsed downstream has acquired an unversioned output surface.

supportBundles.rule: User-triggered only, privacy-classed per artifact, with a manifest listing exactly what is included.
supportBundles.defaults: No source bytes, no credentials, no untracked blobs. Redaction is by CLASS, never by pattern-matching for things that look secret.

validationGates.principle: A gate that can pass while the property it protects is broken is worse than no gate, because it converts an unknown into a false assurance.

gates.asserts: Canonical workflows over fixed corpora reproduce byte-identical digests under identical identities and exact Coverage
gates.note: The single most load-bearing gate: it is the executable form of the determinism claim.

gates.asserts: Every rule's fixture verdicts are unchanged, or the change is explicitly accepted
gates.note: This is where calibration lives. Rule mechanics port cheaply; calibration does not, so it needs a gate of its own.

gates.asserts: Each language provider satisfies the provider protocol and reports fact quality honestly, including unavailability
Subject identities do not drift unintentionally; intentional drift ships with a migrator and a dual-emit window
gates.note: Protects the one contract whose artifacts live in user repositories.

gates.asserts: artifacts/check-d9.py passes: schema, payload, vocabulary closure, derivation, class coverage, finalization
PS-09 and LN-11/LN-12 pass — no tier obtains authority it was not granted, by label or by ambient access
Busy-timeout, disk-full, CAS link failure, process hang, cancel mid-publish each fail closed with a typed outcome and never a passing empty Run
LN-09 same-project contention: each contender publishes or returns typed busy-timeout; no lost or partial writes
Every surface resolves the same Run and Finding identities for one Run
artifacts/check-threat-claims.py passes — no unqualified confinement language anywhere
artifacts/check-claims.py passes — no claim is presented above its registered status
Published capacity-class SLOs are met on a reference corpus
gates.why: Not blocking because no SLO has been measured yet. It becomes blocking once figures exist rather than being asserted.

gates.asserts: If more than one execution lifetime ships, both produce identical digests for identical Plans
gates.why: Conditional on R-1 items 2-4, which are measurement-gated and unresolved.

flakePolicy.rule: An intermittent failure is a bug report, triaged to one terminal outcome: a permanent fix of the product defect or of the test's synchronisation; a deterministic alternative proving the same invariant, after which the timing-dependent form is deleted; or deletion when covered elsewhere.
prohibited: repeat nursing of the same test
flakePolicy.why: A flaky gate teaches the team to ignore gate failures, which disables every other gate in this table.

gateOnGates.rule: Each gate must have a demonstrated failing case — a mutation that the gate catches. A gate never observed to fail is not evidence that the property holds; it is evidence the gate might be vacuous.
gateOnGates.status: Only three of thirteen currently have one: check-d9, check-claims, and check-threat-claims each have a self-test or a recorded catch. The other ten are unproven as gates.

conformanceTests.assert: No plane other than evidence can influence a verdict; a Run computed with recording sinks and with no-op sinks yields identical digests.
Every emitted event across all planes carries a resolvable ExecutionId.
Exceeding a diagnostics budget produces a typed truncation marker naming what was dropped; nothing is silently omitted.
With no exporter configured, local profiling still works and no network call is attempted.
A support bundle contains no source bytes, credentials, or untracked blobs by default, and carries a manifest of included classes.
Producer stderr never appears in a machine-readable output document as a structured field.
Each blocking gate in `gates` has a recorded mutation that it catches (gateOnGates).

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: calibration is protected independently of mechanics
no claim exceeds its registered status

peerReviewRequired: Is G12 correctly non-blocking? Shipping without a performance gate is a real risk, but making an unmeasured SLO blocking would be worse — it would be a gate with no defined pass condition.
gateOnGates says ten of thirteen gates are unproven. Should that block release on its own, given the stated principle that an unproven gate may be vacuous?
Is four planes the right decomposition, or do diagnostics and progress collapse into one with a durability flag?
knownLimitations: Ten of thirteen gates have no demonstrated failing case, which by this artifact's own stated principle means they are unproven as gates. That is recorded rather than resolved.
No SLO figures exist, so G12 has no pass condition.
Budget numbers are not specified — the rule says budgets exist, not what they are.
